result.title: Predicting Process-Level Behavior: A Benchmarking Study
result.comment: Accepted as main track paper at International Conference on Process Mining (ICPM) 2027
result.summary: Predictive process monitoring (PPM) typically forecasts the future of individual process instances, hence operating on trace level. Process managers, however, typically operate on process level, e.g., when assigning staff or calculating KPIs. The question is how well such process-level managerial decisions are supported by existing approaches, given that PPM research has so far not focused on process-level predictions. We answer this question through a comprehensive benchmarking study of two process-level prediction tasks: concurrent trace prediction and average throughput time prediction. Across synthetic and real-life event logs, we compare statistical and machine-learning-based methods, foundation models, business process simulation, and, importantly, established trace-level PPM approaches, aggregating their predictions to the process-level. We assess which modeling paradigms are most suitable for predicting process-level behavior and whether existing trace-level PPM can be effectively repurposed for this task. Our results show substantial variation in performance across approaches. Notably, aggregated trace-level predictions cause errors to compound on process-level, reducing accuracy and highlighting process-level prediction as a distinct predictive task that warrants dedicated research.

AI.brief_summary: 该文是流程挖掘领域的基准研究，比较统计方法、机器学习、基础模型、流程仿真与既有 trace 级预测方法在「并发轨迹预测」和「平均吞吐时间预测」两个流程级任务上的表现，并指出聚合 trace 级预测会导致误差累积。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是业务流程实例的未来演化预测，不涉及视觉信息保留、latent 推理状态或答案对 latent 内容的使用；「实例级聚合到流程级出现误差累积」这一发现与 LVR 的表示、停止决策和证据获取无具体可核查的借用线索，故排除。
